chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwa, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The divorced woman may apply kohl, dye (henna), use perfume, and wear whatever clothes she wishes.
Perhaps Allah will bring about after that a [new] matter.
Perhaps she will become pleasing in his eyes, so he will take her back.

key_terms.لَعَلَّ اللَّهَ يُحْدِثُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ أ: Perhaps Allah will bring about after that a matter (Quranic reference for reconciliation)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a divorced woman wearing makeup and perfume during her waiting period?
ai.summary: In the Shia jurisprudential tradition, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the waiting period (Iddah) does not restrict a woman's personal grooming or attire, distinguishing it from the restrictions placed on widows. The underlying wisdom, rooted in the Quranic promise of potential reconciliation, highlights the psychological aspect of remarriage where the husband's renewed attraction plays a key role. This ruling is frequently cited by scholars like Al-Tusi to demonstrate the permissibility of voluntary adornment as a means to facilitate marital restoration.
